$comment: Binding between course capabilities and plugin skills. See docs/PLUGIN-CONTRACT.md. Units declare capabilities; this file is the only place capability -> skill is decided, so a plugin rename costs one edit here rather than twenty in prose. Multi-plugin: a third-party plugin enters the course only when it is the reference implementation of a concept the course already teaches. See docs/PLUGIN-CONTRACT.md section 9.

spec-driven-engineering.note: The course's workflow. Installed in B1, used for everything after.

ponytail.note: Optional. Cited in C1 as a worked guide (the rung ladder), in C3 as a worked inferential sensor (ponytail-review / ponytail-audit), and in C4 as a published ablation with a public correction. Pairs with engineering-standards' YAGNI check rather than replacing it.

workflow-routing.note: Routing table from 'where the work is' to the right skill.

issue-intake.note: Most bad specs start as unexamined tickets.

domain-vocabulary.note: Ambiguous terms produce confident, coherent, wrong software.

spec-authoring.note: The behaviour harness. B1's whole thesis rests on this.

spec-pressure-test.note: Also used on rollout plans in D4.

architecture-lens.note: Same lens before code exists and after.

code-standards.note: C3 exists partly because this states rules nothing enforces.

spec-axis-review.note: Two-axis review; reports a missing spec rather than assuming it satisfied.

conflict-resolution.note: Becomes critical the moment parallel worktrees are in play.

agent-authoring.note: Governs how the reader authors AGENTS.md, docs, and their own skills.

overbuild-audit.note: An inferential sensor for over-engineering, run against a diff or a whole repo. C3 uses it as the worked example of a sensor you did not write; C4 uses its benchmark as the worked example of an honest ablation.

minimality-guide.note: The rung ladder is a feedforward guide in the Bockeler sense - it steers before the agent writes, rather than grading after.

expected_gaps.$comment: Capabilities the curriculum reaches for that the plugin does not yet provide. Not errors. See docs/SKILLS-MAP.md gap analysis. When one of these lands in the plugin, move it into capabilities and follow the intake process in docs/PLUGIN-CONTRACT.md section 3.

spec-linting.note: Highest priority. spec-from-idea currently emits criteria nothing checks.

repo-comprehension.note: Onboarding an agent to a large existing codebase. No skill in the plugin covers brownfield comprehension; codebase-architecture assumes you already understand the shape.
